saturation.stopReason: French Open Government and final CNSC, CNL, fuel, transport and customer searches produced no additional decision-changing field after the consolidated LEUNR candidate captured the material design, maturity, program, partner and continuity evidence.

warnings: Corporations Canada lists CSMC as Active but flags two consecutive overdue annual filings and a notice of intent to dissolve; recheck immediately before any publication decision.
No reviewed public source establishes a CNSC vendor design review, licence application, approved site, environmental review, fueled criticality or operating reactor for CSMC or LEUNR.
CSA describes TRL 4/5 conceptual design moving toward TRL 6 detailed design; a company-stated July 2026 TRL 5 deadline has no public completion proof.
The NRC IRAP record defines an unfuelled instrumentation-and-controls prototype objective but publishes no completion or acceptance result.
OECD-NEA's 0.1 MWth, 130 C and fuel parameters are a 2025 historical design basis and require confirmation before buyer use.
No public CSMC agreement establishes qualified HALEU supply, fuel fabrication, reservation or delivery.
Telesat's arrangement is an MOU; pilots and commercial or operational arrangements require definitive agreements.
NGen funds manufacturing-process and factory-cell development, not a proven serial line or tens-to-hundreds annual production capacity.
ERA and the University of Alberta describe an unfuelled prototype or physical simulator, not a fueled reactor, criticality event or licensed facility.
Public contributions and total-project values have different bases and are deliberately not aggregated as financing or revenue.
The Canadian Explorers article is an attributed CEO interview, not independent proof of size, transportability, refuelling interval, output, manufacturing capacity, financing or deployment.
No named Indigenous community, northern utility, defence installation or site owner is publicly established as a LEUNR customer, consent partner or deployment host.
A peer-reviewed CNL-authored paper raises lunar heat-rejection limits for low-temperature light-water concepts but does not test LEUNR or establish terrestrial Arctic infeasibility.
